item.title: Blue states push to ban ICE at the polls amid federal voter intimidation fears
item.description: Several Democratic states are moving to bar federal immigration agents from being near polling places and other election sites, amid persistent worries that President Donald Trump will use federal law enforcement or the military to disrupt the midterm elections.

item.title: Man accused of starting Palisades fire should be released after Lachman fire revelations, attorney says
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The attorney representing the man accused of starting the Lachman fire before it turned into the deadly Palisades fire is demanding the immediate release of his client following a sworn deposition by a Los Angeles city firefighter who testified that he told co-workers and a captain that the first fire was not fully out as they packed up hoses on Jan. 2.

item.title: Florida taxpayers likely on the hook for Alligator Alcatraz
item.description: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Gov. Ron DeSantis proclaimed on social media in early October that the federal government had awarded the state $608 million to help recoup the cost of building Alligator Alcatraz.

item.title: From orchard to market: Columbia Fruit Packers demonstrates apple production, export
item.description: Behind the doors at Columbia Fruit Packers, the air felt different: cooler, metallic, alive with motion. Apples were everywhere and nowhere at once: floating in water, rolling under cameras, disappearing into boxes and bags bound for places far beyond the valley.

item.title: Federal aid for lead cleanup is receding. That’s a problem for cash-strapped cities
item.description: Tighter regulations and an influx of federal money in recent years have helped communities across the U.S. initiate efforts to clean up lead contamination in soil, drinking water, and older homes. But Congress and the Trump administration have partially rolled back those rules and resources, potentially making it more challenging for cash-strapped cities and towns to undertake sweeping lead remediation programs.

item.title: 3A Girls Basketball State Fourth-place Game: Evergreen takes sixth place for best finish in program history
item.description: "Everyone (did) their jobs," coach Dexteur Lesueur said. "From the coaches, to the players, to the boosters, Evergreen admin, staff (and) community, everyone is uplifting. When you have that type of culture of uplifting, anything is possible. The sky is the limit. I'm just happy that we had everybody backing us and believing in us."

item.title: 2A Boys Basketball State Championship: Jalen Davis hits two late free throws to lift Bremerton over R.A. Long 45-43
item.description: Jalen Davis hit two free throws with 4.4 seconds to lift Bremerton to a second straight state title, beating R.A. Long 45-43 in the 2A boys basketball state championship game Saturday at the Yakima Valley SunDome.
